cases.prompt: I just got a brand new MacBook, what do I need to install before Homebrew?
install the Xcode command line tools
xcode-select --install failed, help me get the CLT set up properly
do i need rosetta on my m4 mac? set it up if so
prep this fresh mac so I can start installing dev tools
git says invalid active developer path after the macOS upgrade
update macos and get the developer toolchain baseline ready
clang: command not found on my new mac
where should I keep my source code on a new mac, and get the basics ready
install homebrew for me
enable filevault and touch id for sudo
install full Xcode with iOS simulators
show hidden files in Finder and speed up key repeat
set up my whole new mac for development end to end
upgrade all my brew packages and update everything
my xcode build fails with a code signing error
set up an ubuntu VM on my mac
Get my brand-new M3 MacBook ready so I can start installing developer tools.
expected_behavior: checks for pending macOS updates first and asks the user to install them (with restart warning) before anything else
installs Xcode Command Line Tools via xcode-select --install, waits for the GUI installer, and verifies with xcode-select -p
offers Rosetta 2 install on Apple Silicon as optional, explaining the macOS 27/28 sunset, and uses softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license only with consent
does not install Homebrew or any packages, pointing to the homebrew-setup skill as the next step
verifies each step with a read-only command before declaring done

cases.prompt: git stopped working after I upgraded macOS — it says invalid active developer path.
expected_behavior: diagnoses the missing/stale Command Line Tools rather than reinstalling git
re-runs xcode-select --install (or resets CLT) and verifies with xcode-select -p and git --version
mentions that macOS major upgrades invalidate or reset the CLT and this recurs

cases.prompt: Do I actually need Rosetta 2 on this Apple Silicon Mac?
expected_behavior: explains Rosetta is only needed for remaining Intel-only apps/binaries and is being phased out (general-purpose through macOS 27, narrowed in macOS 28)
recommends installing on demand rather than preemptively, and shows the softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license command
does not run the install without user consent

cases.prompt: asdf just tell me the exact first steps on a factory-reset mac before i can brew install stuff
expected_behavior: gives the ordered sequence: Software Update first, then Xcode CLT, then (optional) Rosetta, then hand off to Homebrew
warns not to run the CLT installer and the Homebrew installer in parallel
keeps the answer focused on prep; no package installs
